note: Guernsey: a worker who isn't locally qualified takes up a job under an Employment Permit of the Population Management regime, a Short Term Employment Permit for up to 12 months at a time; a British or Irish national needs only that, anyone else a valid immigration status as well, a work visa since the end of free movement with the EU (States of Guernsey, Employment Permit FAQ). No days of work without either are named.

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Employment Permit Policy FAQ
sources.said: Short Term Employment Permits will continue to be issued for up to 12 months, renewable upon expiry. ... As a result of Brexit and the end of 40 years of free movement between the UK/Islands and the EU/EEA/Switzerland, anyone who is not a British or Irish national needs to hold a valid immigration status. This means that any new EU/EEA/Swiss nationals now need to apply for a visa to live and work in Guernsey.
